origins.section: Cipher.getInstance("AES") Is ECB, and ECB Encrypts Equal Blocks to Equal Blocks
A GCM IV Used Twice Under One Key Gives Away the XOR of the Two Plaintexts
A Password Hash Needs a Salt per User and a Slow Function: PBKDF2, Not SHA-256
Compare Tags and Hashes with MessageDigest.isEqual; Arrays.equals Stops at the First Difference

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-mode-not-named: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mode-not-named: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mode-not-named: Section 'Cipher.getInstance("AES") Is ECB...': 'SunJCE picks ECB with PKCS5 padding, with no IV and no tag' and 'ECB encrypts each 16-byte block independently under the key, so block 2 equals block 0'; the output shows '"AES" (no mode named)' giving identical blocks 0 and 2 and 'getIV(): null'. Reference table: 'Cipher.getInstance("AES") | AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding; getIV() is null'. With equal fixed-length lines (same padding too), a reader concludes identical stored bytes produced from the key alone. Minor inferential step: the page's demo encrypts all three records in one call, not with a re-init per line, but 'independently under the key' with no IV covers it.
recorded.prompt:q-iv-drawn-once: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-iv-drawn-once: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-iv-drawn-once: Section 'A GCM IV Used Twice Under One Key Gives Away the XOR of the Two Plaintexts': the scenario matches the stem ('drew its IV from SecureRandom, once ... a new Cipher for each'), the output shows 'c1 xor c2' equal to 'p1 xor p2', and the text says 'The keystream depends only on the key and the IV, so the same pair gives the same keystream, and XOR-ing the two ciphertexts cancels it. What remains is the XOR of the plaintexts, computed without the key'.
recorded.prompt:q-salt-without-cost: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-salt-without-cost: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-salt-without-cost: Section 'A Password Hash Needs a Salt per User and a Slow Function': 'A salt doesn't make a single guess any slower. The iteration count does', and 'A salt per user makes equal passwords look different, so no precomputed table matches'. Both halves of the option (same work per guess, different matching digests) are stated. The page never shows salted single-pass SHA-256 itself, but these sentences settle it.
recorded.prompt:q-tag-comparison: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-tag-comparison: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-tag-comparison: Section 'Compare Tags and Hashes with MessageDigest.isEqual...': the six-row table gives the same answers for both checks, then 'The answers match; the difference is the running time.' Arrays.equals in JDK 21 'returns as soon as the lengths differ or a difference is found'; isEqual's 'calculation time depends only on the length of digesta'. Summary: 'same answers as Arrays.equals, but its time doesn't depend on where the bytes differ.'

recorded.prompt:q-mode-not-named:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mode-not-named:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mode-not-named:b: Same section: plain "AES" is ECB 'with no IV and no tag', and the run prints 'getIV(): null'. There is no IV to reuse.
recorded.prompt:q-mode-not-named:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mode-not-named:c: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mode-not-named:c: Same section: "AES" means ECB with 'no IV' ('getIV(): null'), and its identical blocks 0 and 2 show the output is not randomised. The provider-drawn IV appears only for GCM (Reference: 'GCM init(ENCRYPT_MODE, key) with no parameters | provider draws a 12-byte IV').
recorded.prompt:q-mode-not-named:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-mode-not-named:d: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-mode-not-named:d: Same section: 'ECB encrypts each 16-byte block independently under the key', with no IV, so the output depends only on key and block. The page never states outright that re-initialising leaves the output unchanged; a reader has to infer it from the 'independently under the key' wording. Refuted by inference, not by a shown run.

The stem says a new Cipher per message, so no exception.
